clue.text: Old country merchant investing initially in tea

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the initials go inside the tea

parts.note: Bohea is a black China tea, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letters of the words merchant and in

explanation.surface: A trader with a stake in tea from some former nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' applies to both 'merchant' and 'in', so two initials go inside the tea; Bohea is an old name for a black China tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia was a historic kingdom in central Europe, now the western part of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Rumbling sound made by floating barrier

definitions.meaning: a deep resonant noise, like distant thunder
a chain of floating logs or beams stretched across a harbour or river

explanation.definitionFit: Both a deep resonant noise and a floating harbour barrier share this one four-letter word.

clue.text: Crude shelter in which a politician's stored fish

indicators.note: stored means kept inside, so the politician goes into the shelter

parts.note: a hut is a rough simple shelter
Lib is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A Liberal keeps a fish hidden in a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish of northern seas, a common food fish.

clue.text: Dynamic type making mass deliveries

parts.note: M is the standard symbol for mass in physics
in cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by one bowler

explanation.surface: An energetic courier handling bulk parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests post, but it is cricket: an over is six balls bowled in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A mover is a person who gets things going, an energetic, dynamic sort, as in movers and shakers.

clue.text: Sort of shirt soldier used in anti-aircraft defence

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, so shirt and soldier go between the two letters

parts.note: a polo shirt is a short-sleeved collared top
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier's shirt is part of the air-defence kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's opinions or conduct, as in Newman's Apologia.

clue.text: Fruit increased in value with it

parts.note: shares that rose went up in price
hip means fashionable, up to date

explanation.surface: Some produce has gone up in price, and it's trendy too.
explanation.definitionFit: The hip is the red berry-like fruit of the wild rose, used for syrup.

clue.text: Less cautious breakfast selection?

definitions.meaning: more reckless, the comparative of a word for hasty
a slice of bacon chosen for a fried breakfast

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of rash means more reckless, and a homonym is a single slice of bacon or ham.

clue.text: Cheeky display from poet with pretentious air?.

parts.note: side is an old British word for swagger or putting on airs
Robert Burns, the Scottish national poet

explanation.surface: A bard puts on airs with a cheeky performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky' is a pun: hair grown down the cheeks. 'With' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of whisker grown down the sides of the face, a display on the cheeks.

clue.text: Married man, losing heart, has oddly substituted cradle song

indicators.note: the middle letter of the husband word is dropped
oddly says the letters of has are jumbled, and substituted says they go where the lost letter stood

parts.note: hubby is a colloquial word for a husband
the letters of has, mixed up, put in the gap

explanation.surface: A husband, out of sorts, swaps in a lullaby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' drops the middle B of HUBBY, and 'oddly' turns HAS into SHA, which is 'substituted' in its place: HU-SHA-BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hushaby is a soothing word sung to lull a baby to sleep, hence a lullaby.

clue.text: Hiker's flat

explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian is a walker, and the adjective means dull and lacking imagination.

clue.text: Unaware of Light Infantry invading plain

indicators.note: invading means getting inside, so the troops go into the other word

parts.note: plain means clear, evident
LI is the military abbreviation for Light Infantry

explanation.surface: Troops storm the flatlands without noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like open country but means evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivious means not aware of what is happening around one.

clue.text: Given medicine 12's man rejected after party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: the man in the wordplay of 12 down is Des, a short form of Desmond

explanation.surface: A man spurned after a party is given some medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosed means given a measured amount of a drug or remedy.

clue.text: Make irrevocable commitment to finish off own gigs?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for acting so that there is no way to retreat
a gig is also a light rowing boat, so setting fire to one's own craft

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from setting fire to your own boats so there is no retreat, taking a step that cannot be undone.

clue.text: Unexpectedly called to hold unknown man's horse

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the rearranged word wraps the other letters
unexpectedly signals that the letters of called come out in a surprising order

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown
Des is a short form of the name Desmond

explanation.surface: A man's horse was summoned without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' reworks the letters of the word called, and 'to hold' wraps that around the unknown and the man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Clydesdale is a heavy Scottish breed of draught horse.

clue.text: Seducer reluctant to take a port

parts.note: loth means unwilling
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A womaniser is unwilling to go to a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, the rake in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, became a byword for a womaniser.

clue.text: Petition from person settling across river

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the payer word straddles the letter

parts.note: a payer is someone who settles a bill
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A request from someone paying up across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest request, as to God or to a court, the same as a petition.

clue.text: Grasping fellow surgeons touring Oxford University

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning fellow, joint, as in co-worker

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the surgeons surround the university

parts.note: vets are animal surgeons

explanation.surface: A greedy colleague and some surgeons on a visit to Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Covetous means eager to possess things, greedy, which is a figurative sense of grasping.

clue.text: Run out on infertile land

definitions.meaning: abandon or leave in the lurch

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means abandon, and as a noun it means arid barren terrain.

clue.text: In verse, tell about ancient city originally famous for sport

indicators.note: about means going round, so the verb surrounds the city and the initial

parts.note: to sing is to tell a story in poetry, as in Arms and the man I sing
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letter of famous

explanation.surface: A poem recounts an ancient city once famous for a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Surfing is the water sport of riding waves on a board.

clue.text: Dessert out East also known as main course in Greece

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter leaves the pudding

parts.note: a mousse is a light whipped pudding
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A pudding from the East is also served as a Greek entree.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits dessert against main course, but the pudding only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a baked Greek dish of aubergine, minced meat and white sauce, eaten as a main dish.

clue.text: Each of us may reject wine without this

definitions.text: Each of us may reject wine without this

parts.words: Each of us may reject wine without this
parts.note: wine said to lack body is thin, so the clue reads as any of us turning down wine short of this fullness, while the whole phrase means every person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means any person at all, each of us, and splits as a qualifier plus the fullness wine needs.

clue.text: Cooked slowly and canned

explanation.definitionFit: It means braised gently, and is also British slang for very drunk.

clue.text: When tossers expect to have a pancake landing?

definitions.text: When tossers expect to have a pancake landing?

parts.words: When tossers expect to have a pancake landing?
parts.note: a pancake landing is an aircraft belly-flop, but here it is pancakes flipped in the pan landing back in it on the traditional day

explanation.definitionFit: Pancakes are traditionally tossed on this day before Lent begins, also called Pancake Day.

clue.text: The aspiration of Gerontius and Olwen?

definitions.text: The aspiration of Gerontius and Olwen?

parts.words: The aspiration of Gerontius and Olwen?
parts.note: Elgar's oratorio about Gerontius and Charles Williams's piano piece for Olwen share a title word that also means a hope

explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is a cherished hope, and the word names both Elgar's oratorio and the 1947 film piano piece.

clue.text: Paid to eat

definitions.meaning: having had a fee given, a humorous verb from the noun fee
of animals, to take food, as cattle do on grass

explanation.definitionFit: Read as fee'd it means paid a fee, and as a verb of animals it means take food.

clue.text: Part of 23 is seriously faulty

indicators.note: part of signals that the letters lie within the run of words, with 23 read as its answer

explanation.surface: Something in the aspiration is badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Write in the answer to 23 down and the run reads DRE-AM IS S-eriously, holding the letters; 'seriously' is an intensifier on the surface but only lends its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrong or faulty, as in something is amiss.

clue.text: Healthy ladies haven't finished digesting parts of course

indicators.note: digesting means taking inside, so the trimmed word swallows the holes
the last letter of the women word is dropped

parts.note: women is a synonym for ladies
a golf course is made up of eighteen holes

explanation.surface: Ladies who haven't finished their meal are working through the courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a meal course but is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesome means good for health or well-being, as in wholesome food.

clue.text: No shock, presumably, for such an intellectual?

definitions.text: No shock, presumably, for such an intellectual?

parts.words: No shock, presumably, for such an intellectual?
parts.note: a shock is a mass of hair, and a bald domed head suggests an egg

explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is a highbrow, named for the supposed bald dome of thinkers.

clue.text: Dog retired graduate's last to identify in dictionary

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate, so the possessive gives MAS

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the dictionary abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of identify

explanation.surface: Naming a dog, a retired graduate looks it up in the dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns MAS into SAM, and 'last' takes Y from 'identify', which goes 'in' OED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a white Siberian spitz breed of dog.
